pairs.evidence: src/lib/visual-gen/tripo-job-store.ts:86 Generation jobs outlive the turn that submits them, and the model polls them through pof_asset_generate_status, but their only record is an in-process Map, so a server restart turns every outstanding jobId into a not-found while paid provider tasks keep running.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/visual-gen/tripo-job-store.ts:2 No durable row is written before the job id goes back. The caller or model keeps the id and polls, and the store does not survive a restart. The triposr, hunyuan and trellis stores use the same in-memory Map pattern.

src/lib/visual-gen/tripo-job-store.ts:47 When polling ends while the paid task is still live, the outcome is unknown, yet the job is closed as status 'error' with a side flag (recoverable = true at line 204). The status list has no unknown value, so a reader that checks only status sees a failure. Refusing to re-roll a live task does match the technique's metered-generation rule.

pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/evaluator/WorkflowOrchestratorView/ExecutionHistoryRow.tsx:11 A workflow run whose owning process vanished is stored with status 'failed', and the history row has to look at a side field to recover that the outcome was actually unknown. Any consumer that counts status 'failed' books interruptions as failures.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/evaluator/WorkflowOrchestratorView/index.tsx:52 The technique says to add a first-class indeterminate status when the list lacks one. The store (taskDAGStore.demoteInterrupted, outside this context) instead writes 'failed' plus failureReason 'reload-interrupted', and this context's views special-case it.
